<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par72" />''and he took away'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=13}}. The 1st ''sing.'' of the {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}} commonly has the form {{GHGheb|text=וָאָֽשִׁ֫יב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=2|verse=20}}, or, more often, defectively {{GHGheb|text=וָאָֽעִד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=42}}, less frequently the form {{GHGheb|text=וָאָֽשֵׁב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=14|verse=7}}.—For {{GHGheb|text=אָסֵף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=1|verse=2}} (after {{GHGheb|text=אָסֹף}}) and in verse 3, read {{GHGheb|text=אֹסֵף}} from {{GHGheb|text=אָסַף}}, on the analogy of {{GHGheb|text=אֹמֵד}} {{GHGpar|68|g}}: similarly in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=8|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽסְפֵם}} instead of {{GHGheb|text=אֲסִיפֵם}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|bb}}
In the {{GHGterm|imperfect Pôlēl}} the tone is moved backwards before a following tone-syllable, but without a shortening of the vowel of the final syllable; e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תְּר֫וֹמֵֽם גּ֑וֹי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=14|verse=34}}; {{GHGheb|text=תְּח֫וֹלֵֽל לוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=35|verse=14}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=23}}, and acc. to Baer {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּתְבֹּ֫נֵֽן בִּֽי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=20}} (ed. Mant., Ginsb. {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּתְבֹּנֶן בִּֽי}}), always in principal pause; on the {{GHGterm|Metheg}} with {{GHGterm|Ṣere}}, cf. {{GHGpar|16|f}} γ.—As ''Pôlal'' cf. {{GHGheb|text=יְרֹעָ֑ע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=16|verse=10}}.

As {{GHGterm|participle Hophʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=הַמּוּשַׁב}} occurs in close connexion, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=12}}; cf. {{GHGpar|65|d}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|cc}}
Peculiar contracted forms of ''Pôlēl'' (unless they are transitives in {{GHGterm|Qal}}) are {{GHGheb|text=וַיְכֻנֶ֫נּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=15}}, {{GHGheb|text=יְעוּרֶ֫נּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=41|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּמוּגֵ֫נוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=64|verse=6}} for {{GHGheb|text=וַיְכֹֽנְנֶ֫נּוּ}}, &c. [but read {{GHGheb|text=וַיְכֹנְנֵנוּ}} ({{GHGpar|58|k}}), {{GHGheb|text=יְעִירֶנּוּ}} or {{GHGheb|text=יְעוֹרְנֶנּוּ}}, and {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּמַגְּנֵנוּ}}]; also {{GHGheb|text=תְּרֹמֵם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=17|verse=4}}, for {{GHGheb|text=תְּרֹֽמְמֵם}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=15|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=יְעֹעֵ֫רוּ}} appears to have arisen from the ''Pilpel'' {{GHGheb|text=יְעַרְעֵ֫רוּ}}, the ''ă'' after the loss of the {{GHGheb|text=ר}} having been lengthened to ''ā'', which has then been obscured to ''ô''.—For the strange form {{GHGheb|text=בִּֽתְקֽוֹמֲמֶ֫יךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=21}}, which cannot (according to {{GHGpar|52|s}}) be explained as a {{GHGterm|participle}} with the {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}} omitted, read {{GHGheb|text=בְּמִתְק׳}}.

{{center|IV. ''In General.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|dd}}
8. The verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} are primarily related to the verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} (§ 67), which were also originally biliteral, so that it is especially necessary in analysing them to pay attention to the differences between the inflexion of the two classes. Several forms are exactly the same in both, e.g. {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} with {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}}, the whole of {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}, the ''Piʿlēl'' of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, and the {{GHGterm|Pôʿēl}} of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}; see {{GHGpar|67|z}}. Owing to this close relation, verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} sometimes have forms which follow the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, e.g. {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=בַּז|translate=he has despised}} (from {{GHGheb|text=בּוּז}}, as if from {{GHGheb|text=בָּזַז}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=4|verse=10}}; {{GHGterm|perfect Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נָמָרֽ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=11}} (for {{GHGheb|text=נָמוֹר}} from {{GHGheb|text=מוּר}}, as if from {{GHGheb|text=מָרַר}}). The same explanation equally applies to {{GHGheb|text=נָֽקְטָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=10|verse=1}} for {{GHGheb|text=נָקַ֫טָּה}} (cf. § 67 dd) = {{GHGheb|text=נָק֫וֹטָה}} from {{GHGheb|text=קוּט}}, and {{GHGheb|text=נָ֫קֹטּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=6|verse=9}} (for {{GHGheb|text=נָק֫וֹטוּ}}); {{GHGheb|text=יֵר֫וֹמּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=10|verse=17}} and {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּרֹ֫מּוּ}} verse 15; {{GHGheb|text=הֵרֹ֫מּוּ}} ({{GHGterm|imperative}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִסַּג}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=2|verse=6}}; ''Hiphʿîl perfect'' {{GHGheb|text=הֵתַז}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=18|verse=5}} for {{GHGheb|text=הֵתֵז}} (cf. {{GHGpar|29|q}}), which is for {{GHGheb|text=הֵתִיז}} from {{GHGheb|text=תּוּז}}. On the other hand the ''imperfects'' {{GHGheb|text=יָמֵר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=48|verse=14}} (unless it be intended for {{GHGheb|text=יָמִר}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=15|verse=4}}) and {{GHGheb|text=יָפֵחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=2|verse=3}}, are to be regarded according to {{GHGpar|109|i}}, simply as rhythmically shortened forms of {{GHGheb|text=יָמִיר}} and {{GHGheb|text=יָפִיחַ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|ee}}
9. In common with verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} ({{GHGpar|67|g}}) verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} sometimes have in {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} the quasi-Aramaic formation, by which, instead of the long vowel under the preformative, they take a short vowel with ''Dageš forte'' in the following consonant; this variety is frequently found even along with the ordinary form, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִסִּית|translate=to incite}}, imperfect {{GHGheb|text=יַסִּית}} (also {{GHGheb|text=הֵסִית}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָסִית}}); {{GHGheb|text=הִסִּיג}}, imperfect {{GHGheb|text=יַסִּיג|translate=to remove}} (from {{GHGheb|text=סוּג}}), also {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=הֻסַּג}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=14}} (on {{GHGheb|text=הֻ֣קַּם}} cf. {{GHGpar|29|g}}); sometimes with a difference of meaning, as {{GHGheb|text=הֵנִיחַ|translate=to cause to rest}},<ref>As the passive of this {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} we should expect the {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=הוּנַח}}, which is, no doubt, to be read for {{GHGheb|text=הוּנַּח}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=5|verse=5}}.</ref> but {{GHGheb|text=הִנִּיחַ}} ({{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יַנִּיחַ}}, {{GHGterm|consecutive}} {{GHGheb|text=וַתַּנִּ֫חַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=16}}; {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=הַנַּח}}, ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=הַנִּ֫יחוּ}}) ''to set down''; for {{GHGheb|text=וַהֻנִּ֫יחָה}} (Baer, Ginsburg {{GHGheb|text=וְהֻנִ׳}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=5|verse=11}} (which at any rate could only be explained as an isolated passive of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} on the analogy of the biblical Aramaic {{GHGheb|text=הֳקִימַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=7|verse=4}}) we should probably read {{GHGheb|text=וַהִנִּיחֻ֫הָ}} with
<section end="par72" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
